svg.title: 2. Checkout saga and compensations
svg.text: Saga state table (checkout DB), the orchestrator's memory
Rules that keep a saga honest
The checkout saga: local transactions forward, compensations backward
The orchestrator writes its state before every call, so a crash resumes from the last step instead of starting over.
Left of the line: any failure is undone
Right of the line: no going back. Steps are
retried until they succeed (they are idempotent).
Compensations run in reverse order and are idempotent too.
ask the PSP by idempotency key,
A recovery worker picks up rows stuck IN_PROGRESS for over 30 s and replays that step with the same key.
1. Save the step, then call. Never the other way round.
2. Every step and compensation is idempotent.
5. Shoppers see PENDING; email only on CONFIRMED.
6. Alert on sagas older than 10 minutes.
Choreography (services reacting to each other's events) works for 2 or 3 steps. Past that, an orchestrator
with a state table is far easier to debug at 3 a.m.: one row tells you where every checkout is.
